Continue building Trueup in this repository. Read README.md, hackathon.md and src/ first. This session is recorded by Entire and published, so work only inside this repository and never mention anything outside it. Do not git commit or push.

Reference code: `.ref/` (gitignored) holds a rough harness written earlier today during the event: fake.py/fake2.py (fake OpenAI + Anthropic server, scenario chosen by the request's model name), run.py (26 plain-SDK scenarios) and run2.py (22 framework scenarios). Rebuild it properly inside the package; do not copy it as is.

Task: the truth side.
1. `src/trueup/fake/`: a local HTTP fake provider (stdlib http.server in a thread, or similar; random free port) speaking: OpenAI Chat Completions (plain, streaming with and without usage, tool calls incl. 2 parallel and split streamed arguments, refusal, n=2, HTTP 500, error event mid-stream, dropped connection), OpenAI Responses (plain, function call, reasoning summary, status failed, status incomplete, streaming event sequence, error event, cut), Anthropic Messages (plain, thinking, tool_use with input_json_delta, streaming, error event, cut, 529). Scenario is chosen by the request's model name. Every response id is unique per call. It logs every request and what it sent back (the truth log: number of calls, tokens per call).
2. Fixture tests: each format parsed by the real `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs (add them as dev dependencies) pointed at the fake, asserting the SDK accepts it and the values match. Errors and cuts must raise the SDK's own exceptions.
3. `src/trueup/scenarios/`: the scenario library as data (id, provider/api, framework, what the app does, expected truth fields), starting with the plain-SDK cases (OpenAI chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic). Framework cases (LangChain/LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK) may be listed but marked not_built if time is short; say so honestly.
4. `src/trueup/runner/`: runs one scenario in a fresh subprocess with a target library's recommended setup, captures every exported span in memory (OpenTelemetry InMemorySpanExporter) plus the app outcome (result or exception type and message), and returns an Observation (truth + trace) as JSON. Per-library venvs under `.trueup/venvs/<lib>` created with uv; libraries: neatlogs (neatlogs.init with its openai/anthropic instrumentation, export disabled), openinference (OpenAIInstrumentor, AnthropicInstrumentor), openllmetry (Traceloop.init with an in-memory exporter, disable_batch=True). Memory is limited: build and run one library at a time. A scenario that can't run is reported NOT RUN with the reason, never skipped.
5. Known traps, each needs a regression test: two scenarios reusing a response id makes a library skip a span; reusing one async client across asyncio.run loops gives "Event loop is closed"; a fake that sends no usage makes missing tokens look like a bug; neatlogs export to a dead endpoint makes a run take 200 s.
6. `trueup sweep <library>` runs the plain-SDK scenarios against one library and writes the observations to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/` with a short text summary. Comparing truth to trace is the next step, not this one.
7. Add a dated entry to hackathon.md and update CHANGELOG.md. Plain words, no marketing filler.

Run `uv run pytest -q` (keep unit tests offline and fast; mark venv/subprocess tests as e2e) and then actually run `uv run trueup sweep` for each of the three libraries, one at a time. Finish with a summary: tests passed, scenarios run per library, any NOT RUN with reasons.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

content.content:
Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

Only the skeleton exists. `trueup doctor` works. The other commands (`audit`, `sweep`, `fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no mismatches, 1 mismatches found, 2 could not run.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
uv sync
uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q
```

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
# Build log

neatHack, 10-12 Oct 2026.

## 2026-10-10: skeleton

- Set up the uv project (Python 3.12, src layout) with the `trueup` command.
- Added the data model in `trueup.core`: Observation, Mismatch, Run, Finding and Severity, each with `to_dict`/`from_dict`.
- `trueup doctor` reports the Python version and whether the two keys are set, without printing them. Other commands exit 2 with "not built yet".
- Tests for the round trip, severity order and doctor. CI runs them on push.
- Nothing is audited yet. No findings so far.

toolUseResult.stdout:
Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

Only the skeleton exists. `trueup doctor` works. The other commands (`audit`, `sweep`, `fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no mismatches, 1 mismatches found, 2 could not run.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
uv sync
uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q
```

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

- `trueup doctor` reports the Python version and whether the two keys are set, without printing them. Other commands exit 2 with "not built yet".
- Tests for the round trip, severity order and doctor. CI runs them on push.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import json
import secrets
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class Reply:
    status: int
    body: bytes
    content_type: str = "application/json"
    # Write the body, then drop the connection before the declared length.
    cut: bool = False
    # Truth facts about this reply.
    response_id: str | None = None
    outcome: str = "complete"  # complete, failed, incomplete, error_event, cut, http_error
    usage: dict[str, int] | None = None  # None means the fake sent no usage
    finish: list[str | None] = field(default_factory=list)
    tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    text: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    headers: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def facts(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "status_code": self.status,
            "response_id": self.response_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "usage": dict(self.usage) if self.usage is not None else None,
            "usage_sent": self.usage is not None,
            "finish": list(self.finish),
            "tool_calls": [dict(t) for t in self.tool_calls],
            "text": list(self.text),
        }


class Ids:
    """Ids unique per call and per server instance.

    Reusing a response id across calls makes some libraries treat the second
    span as a duplicate and drop it, so every id carries a per-server token and
    a counter.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._token = secrets.token_hex(4)
        self._count = itertools.count(1)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def new(self, prefix: str) -> str:
        with self._lock:
            n = next(self._count)
        return f"{prefix}{self._token}{n:04d}"


def dumps(obj: Any) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")).encode()


def json_reply(status: int, obj: Any, **kw: Any) -> Reply:
    return Reply(status=status, body=dumps(obj), **kw)


def sse(data: Any, event: str | None = None) -> bytes:
    head = f"event: {event}\n" if event else ""
    payload = data if isinstance(data, str) else json.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":"))
    return f"{head}data: {payload}\n\n".encode()


def stream_reply(parts: list[bytes], **kw: Any) -> Reply:
    return Reply(status=200, body=b"".join(parts), content_type="text/event-stream", **kw)

"""The fake parsed by the real openai and anthropic SDKs.

Each test checks that the SDK accepts what the fake sends, that the values the
app sees match, and that the truth log records the call.
"""

import asyncio
import json

import anthropic
import openai
import pytest

from trueup.fake import FakeProvider

M = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]


@pytest.fixture
def fake():
    with FakeProvider() as f:
        yield f


@pytest.fixture
def oc(fake):
    return openai.OpenAI(api_key="x", base_url=fake.openai_base_url, max_retries=0)


@pytest.fixture
def ac(fake):
    return anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="x", base_url=fake.base_url, max_retries=0)


def only(fake):
    entries = fake.log.entries()
    assert len(entries) == 1
    return entries[0]


# OpenAI Chat Completions


def test_chat_plain(fake, oc):
    r = oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-plain", messages=M)
    assert r.choices[0].message.content == "hello"
    assert r.choices[0].finish_reason == "stop"
    assert (r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens, r.usage.total_tokens) == (11, 7, 18)
    e = only(fake)
    assert e["response_id"] == r.id
    assert e["usage"] == {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 18}
    assert e["api"] == "openai.chat" and e["outcome"] == "complete"


def test_chat_stream_with_usage(fake, oc):
    text, usage, ids = "", None, set()
    for ch in oc.chat.completions.create(
        model="chat-plain", messages=M, stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}
    ):
        ids.add(ch.id)
        usage = ch.usage or usage
        for c in ch.choices:
            text += c.delta.content or ""
    assert text == "hello"
    assert usage.total_tokens == 18
    e = only(fake)
    assert ids == {e["response_id"]}
    assert e["usage_sent"] and e["include_usage"]


def test_chat_stream_without_usage(fake, oc):
    chunks = list(oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-plain", messages=M, stream=True))
    assert all(ch.usage is None for ch in chunks)
    assert "".join(c.delta.content or "" for ch in chunks for c in ch.choices) == "hello"
    e = only(fake)
    assert e["usage"] is None and e["usage_sent"] is False


def test_chat_two_parallel_tool_calls(fake, oc):
    r = oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-tools", messages=M)
    calls = r.choices[0].message.tool_calls
    assert [(c.function.name, json.loads(c.function.arguments)) for c in calls] == [
        ("get_weather", {"city": "Lagos"}),
        ("get_time", {"tz": "WAT"}),
    ]
    assert r.choices[0].finish_reason == "tool_calls"
    assert calls[0].id != calls[1].id
    assert [t["id"] for t in only(fake)["tool_calls"]] == [c.id for c in calls]


def test_chat_stream_tool_calls_split_arguments(fake, oc):
    calls, finish = {}, None
    for ch in oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-tools", messages=M, stream=True):
        for c in ch.choices:
            finish = c.finish_reason or finish
            for tc in c.delta.tool_calls or []:
                d = calls.setdefault(tc.index, {"id": None, "name": "", "args": ""})
                d["id"] = tc.id or d["id"]
                d["name"] += tc.function.name or ""
                d["args"] += tc.function.arguments or ""
    assert finish == "tool_calls"
    assert [(d["name"], json.loads(d["args"])) for d in calls.values()] == [
        ("get_weather", {"city": "Lagos"}),
        ("get_time", {"tz": "WAT"}),
    ]
    assert [t["arguments"] for t in only(fake)["tool_calls"]] == [d["args"] for d in calls.values()]


def test_chat_refusal(fake, oc):
    r = oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-refusal", messages=M)
    assert r.choices[0].message.content is None
    assert r.choices[0].message.refusal == "I can't help with that."
    chunks = list(oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-refusal", messages=M, stream=True))
    assert "".join(c.delta.refusal or "" for ch in chunks for c in ch.choices) == "I can't help with that."


def test_chat_n2(fake, oc):
    r = oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-n2", messages=M, n=2)
    assert [c.message.content for c in r.choices] == ["one", "two"]
    assert only(fake)["n"] == 2


def test_chat_http_500_raises_sdk_error(fake, oc):
    with pytest.raises(openai.InternalServerError) as e:
        oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-500", messages=M)
    assert e.value.status_code == 500
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "http_error"


def test_chat_error_event_mid_stream_raises_sdk_error(fake, oc):
    text = ""
    with pytest.raises(openai.APIError, match="fake stream error"):
        for ch in oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-error-event", messages=M, stream=True):
            for c in ch.choices:
                text += c.delta.content or ""
    assert text == "hel"
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "error_event"


def test_chat_dropped_connection_raises_sdk_error(fake, oc):
    with pytest.raises(openai.APIConnectionError):
        for _ in oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-cut", messages=M, stream=True):
            pass
    with pytest.raises(openai.APIConnectionError):
        oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-cut", messages=M)
    assert [e["outcome"] for e in fake.log.entries()] == ["cut", "cut"]


# OpenAI Responses


def test_responses_plain(fake, oc):
    r = oc.responses.create(model="resp-plain", input="hi")
    assert r.status == "completed" and r.output_text == "hello"
    assert (r.usage.input_tokens, r.usage.output_tokens) == (11, 7)
    assert only(fake)["response_id"] == r.id


def test_responses_function_call(fake, oc):
    r = oc.responses.create(model="resp-tool", input="hi")
    (fc,) = r.output
    assert fc.type == "function_call" and fc.name == "get_weather"
    assert json.loads(fc.arguments) == {"city": "Lagos"}
    assert only(fake)["tool_calls"][0]["id"] == fc.call_id


def test_responses_reasoning_summary(fake, oc):
    r = oc.responses.create(model="resp-reasoning", input="hi")
    assert [o.type for o in r.output] == ["reasoning", "message"]
    assert r.output[0].summary[0].text == "Think about the weather."
    assert r.usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens == 4
    assert only(fake)["usage"]["reasoning_tokens"] == 4


def test_responses_failed(fake, oc):
    r = oc.responses.create(model="resp-failed", input="hi")
    assert r.status == "failed" and r.error.code == "server_error"
    assert r.output == []
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "failed"


def test_responses_incomplete(fake, oc):
    r = oc.responses.create(model="resp-incomplete", input="hi")
    assert r.status == "incomplete"
    assert r.incomplete_details.reason == "max_output_tokens"
    assert r.output_text == "The answer is cut"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scenario", ["resp-plain", "resp-tool", "resp-reasoning"])
def test_responses_stream_helper_matches_plain(fake, oc, scenario):
    plain = oc.responses.create(model=scenario, input="hi")
    with oc.responses.stream(model=scenario, input="hi") as s:
        types = [ev.type for ev in s]
        final = s.get_final_response()
    assert types[:2] == ["response.created", "response.in_progress"]
    assert types[-1] == "response.completed"
    assert [o.type for o in final.output] == [o.type for o in plain.output]
    assert final.output_text == plain.output_text
    assert final.usage.total_tokens == 18
    assert final.id != plain.id


def test_responses_stream_sequence_numbers_increase(fake, oc):
    seqs = [ev.sequence_number for ev in oc.responses.create(model="resp-reasoning", input="hi", stream=True)]
    assert seqs == list(range(len(seqs)))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("scenario", "last"), [("resp-failed", "response.failed"), ("resp-incomplete", "response.incomplete")])
def test_responses_stream_terminal_status(fake, oc, scenario, last):
    events = list(oc.responses.create(model=scenario, input="hi", stream=True))
    assert events[-1].type == last
    assert events[-1].response.status == scenario.removeprefix("resp-")


def test_responses_stream_error_event_reaches_app(fake, oc):
    # The openai SDK does not raise on a Responses `error` event; it hands
    # the event to the app. Truth records it as an error.
    events = list(oc.responses.create(model="resp-error-event", input="hi", stream=True))
    assert events[-1].type == "error"
    assert events[-1].message == "fake stream error"
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "error_event"


def test_responses_stream_cut_raises_sdk_error(fake, oc):
    with pytest.raises(openai.APIConnectionError):
        for _ in oc.responses.create(model="resp-cut", input="hi", stream=True):
            pass
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "cut"


# Anthropic Messages


def test_anthropic_plain(fake, ac):
    r = ac.messages.create(model="anth-plain", max_tokens=50, messages=M)
    assert r.content[0].text == "hello" and r.stop_reason == "end_turn"
    assert (r.usage.input_tokens, r.usage.output_tokens) == (5, 3)
    assert only(fake)["response_id"] == r.id


def test_anthropic_thinking(fake, ac):
    r = ac.messages.create(model="anth-thinking", max_tokens=50, messages=M)
    assert [b.type for b in r.content] == ["thinking", "text"]
    assert r.content[0].thinking == "Need the weather."


def test_anthropic_stream_helper(fake, ac):
    with ac.messages.stream(model="anth-thinking", max_tokens=50, messages=M) as s:
        text = "".join(s.text_stream)
        final = s.get_final_message()
    assert text == "hello"
    assert [b.type for b in final.content] == ["thinking", "text"]
    assert final.content[0].signature == "fake-sig"
    assert (final.usage.input_tokens, final.usage.output_tokens) == (5, 3)
    assert only(fake)["response_id"] == final.id


def test_anthropic_tool_use_input_json_delta(fake, ac):
    with ac.messages.stream(model="anth-tools", max_tokens=50, messages=M) as s:
        final = s.get_final_message()
    tool = final.content[-1]

    # the event to the app. Truth records it as an error.
    events = list(oc.responses.create(model="resp-error-event", input="hi", stream=True))

    assert events[-1].message == "fake stream error"
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "error_event"

    with pytest.raises(openai.APIConnectionError):

            pass
    assert only(fake)["outcome"] == "cut"

    assert text == "hello"
    assert [b.type for b in final.content] == ["thinking", "text"]
    assert final.content[0].signature == "fake-sig"
    assert (final.usage.input_tokens, final.usage.output_tokens) == (5, 3)
    assert only(fake)["response_id"] == final.id

"""The scenario library, as data.

Each scenario names the fake model it calls (the fake picks its behaviour from

  calls       number of requests the fake received

  exception   exception class name, when outcome is "exception"

  finish      per call: finish/stop reason or response status

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

NOT_BUILT = "not_built"

    api: str  # chat, responses, messages
    framework: str  # none, langchain, langgraph, openai-agents
    does: str  # what the app does, in plain words
    app: str  # function name in trueup.runner.apps
    model: str  # fake scenario, sent as the model name
    expected: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    status: str = BUILT

    @property
    def plain_sdk(self) -> bool:
        return self.framework == "none"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "provider": self.provider,
            "api": self.api,
            "framework": self.framework,
            "does": self.does,
            "app": self.app,
            "model": self.model,
            "expected": self.expected,
            "status": self.status,
        }

    return {
        "calls": calls,
        "outcome": "ok",
        "tokens": [tokens] * calls,
        "finish": [finish] * calls,
        "tool_calls": [tools or []] * calls,
        "fake": [fake] * calls,
    }


def _raises(exc: str, fake: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"calls": 1, "outcome": "exception", "exception": exc, "tokens": [None], "fake": [fake]}


def _s(id: str, provider: str, api: str, does: str, app: str, model: str, expected: dict[str, Any]) -> Scenario:

"""The scenario library, as data.

Each scenario names the fake model it calls (the fake picks its behaviour from
the model name), the app code that drives it (`app`, a function in
trueup.runner.apps), and the truth fields we expect the run to produce.

Expected truth keys (only the ones listed are checked):
  calls       number of requests the fake received
  outcome     "ok" or "exception" (what the app saw)
  exception   exception class name, when outcome is "exception"
  tokens      per call: {"input": n, "output": n}, or None when the fake sent no usage
  finish      per call: finish/stop reason or response status
  tool_calls  per call: tool names the model asked for
  fake        per call: what the fake did (complete, failed, incomplete, error_event, cut, http_error)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

BUILT = "built"
NOT_BUILT = "not_built"

OA_TOK = {"input": 11, "output": 7}
AN_TOK = {"input": 5, "output": 3}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scenario:
    id: str
    provider: str  # openai, anthropic
    api: str  # chat, responses, messages
    framework: str  # none, langchain, langgraph, openai-agents
    does: str  # what the app does, in plain words
    app: str  # function name in trueup.runner.apps
    model: str  # fake scenario, sent as the model name
    expected: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    status: str = BUILT

    @property
    def plain_sdk(self) -> bool:
        return self.framework == "none"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "provider": self.provider,
            "api": self.api,
            "framework": self.framework,
            "does": self.does,
            "app": self.app,
            "model": self.model,
            "expected": self.expected,
            "status": self.status,
        }


def _ok(tokens: Any, finish: Any, tools: Any = None, calls: int = 1, fake: str = "complete") -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "calls": calls,
        "outcome": "ok",
        "tokens": [tokens] * calls,
        "finish": [finish] * calls,
        "tool_calls": [tools or []] * calls,
        "fake": [fake] * calls,
    }


def _raises(exc: str, fake: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"calls": 1, "outcome": "exception", "exception": exc, "tokens": [None], "fake": [fake]}

"""Each target library's recommended setup, wired to an in-memory exporter.

Runs inside the child process, in the library's own venv. Each setup returns
the InMemorySpanExporter and a flush function.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Callable

# Environment for every child. Content capture on, all outbound telemetry off.
CHILD_ENV = {
    "OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT": "true",
    "TRACELOOP_TRACE_CONTENT": "true",
    "TRACELOOP_TELEMETRY": "false",
    # A neatlogs exporter pointed at a dead endpoint retries for ~200 s per run.
    "NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT": "true",
    "OTEL_SDK_DISABLED": "false",
    "OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER": "none",
    "OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER": "none",
    "OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER": "none",
    "OPENAI_API_KEY": "trueup-fake",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "trueup-fake",
}
# Env vars removed from the child so no real key or endpoint is ever used.
CHILD_ENV_DROP = (
    "NEATLOGS_API_KEY",
    "NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT",
    "TRACELOOP_API_KEY",
    "TRACELOOP_BASE_URL",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT",
    "OPENAI_BASE_URL",
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL",
)

# Packages per library venv.
PACKAGES: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs", "openai", "anthropic", "opentelemetry-sdk"],
    "openinference": [
        "openinference-instrumentation-openai",
        "openinference-instrumentation-anthropic",
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "opentelemetry-sdk",
    ],
    "openllmetry": ["traceloop-sdk", "openai", "anthropic"],
}
# Distributions whose versions are recorded with each observation.
VERSIONED: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs", "openai", "anthropic", "opentelemetry-sdk"],
    "openinference": [
        "openinference-instrumentation-openai",
        "openinference-instrumentation-anthropic",
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "opentelemetry-sdk",
    ],
    "openllmetry": [
        "traceloop-sdk",
        "opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai",
        "opentelemetry-instrumentation-anthropic",
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "opentelemetry-sdk",
    ],
}
LIBRARIES = tuple(PACKAGES)


def neatlogs_init_kwargs(tracer_provider: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """neatlogs.init arguments. Export is off and no endpoint is given."""
    return {
        "api_key": "trueup-fake",
        "instrumentations": ["openai", "anthropic"],
        "disable_export": True,
        "tracer_provider": tracer_provider,
        "register_shutdown_handlers": False,
    }


def setup_neatlogs():
    import neatlogs
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    provider = TracerProvider()
    neatlogs.init(**neatlogs_init_kwargs(provider))
    # Added after init so we see spans after neatlogs' own processor ran.
    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))

    def flush() -> None:
        neatlogs.flush(timeout_millis=5000)
        provider.force_flush(5000)

    return exporter, flush


def setup_openinference():
    from openinference.instrumentation.anthropic import AnthropicInstrumentor
    from openinference.instrumentation.openai import OpenAIInstrumentor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    provider = TracerProvider()
    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
    OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    AnthropicInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    return exporter, lambda: provider.force_flush(5000)


def setup_openllmetry():
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
    from traceloop.sdk import Traceloop

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    Traceloop.init(app_name="trueup", exporter=exporter, disable_batch=True, telemetry_enabled=False)

    def flush() -> None:
        from opentelemetry import trace

        p = trace.get_tracer_provider()
        if hasattr(p, "force_flush"):
            p.force_flush(5000)

    return exporter, flush


SETUPS: dict[str, Callable[[], tuple[Any, Callable[[], None]]]] = {
    "neatlogs": setup_neatlogs,
    "openinference": setup_openinference,
    "openllmetry": setup_openllmetry,
}

"""Runs one scenario under one library. Executed in a fresh subprocess.

python -m trueup.runner.child <library> <scenario_id> <out.json>
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import gc
import json
import logging
import sys
import time
import traceback
from importlib import metadata
from typing import Any

from trueup.fake import FakeProvider
from trueup.runner import truth
from trueup.runner.apps import APPS
from trueup.runner.setups import SETUPS, VERSIONED
from trueup.scenarios import get

ATTR_MAX = 2000


def _value(v: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(v, (tuple, list)):
        return [_value(x) for x in v]
    if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > ATTR_MAX:
        return v[:ATTR_MAX] + f"...[{len(v) - ATTR_MAX} more chars]"
    return v


def span_to_dict(s: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ctx = s.get_span_context()
    return {
        "name": s.name,
        "kind": s.kind.name,
        "trace_id": format(ctx.trace_id, "032x"),
        "span_id": format(ctx.span_id, "016x"),
        "parent_id": format(s.parent.span_id, "016x") if s.parent else None,
        "start_ns": s.start_time,
        "end_ns": s.end_time,
        "status": {"code": s.status.status_code.name, "description": s.status.description},
        "scope": s.instrumentation_scope.name if s.instrumentation_scope else None,
        "attributes": {k: _value(v) for k, v in (s.attributes or {}).items()},
        "events": [{"name": e.name, "attributes": {k: _value(v) for k, v in (e.attributes or {}).items()}} for e in s.events],
    }


def _versions(library: str) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    out: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    for dist in VERSIONED[library]:
        try:
            out[dist] = metadata.version(dist)
        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            out[dist] = None
    return out


def run(library: str, scenario_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    scenario = get(scenario_id)
    logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
    exporter, flush = SETUPS[library]()
    app_fn = APPS[scenario.app]
    with FakeProvider() as fake:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = app_fn(fake.base_url, scenario.model)
            app = {"outcome": "ok", "result": result}
        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - the outcome is the data
            app = {
                "outcome": "exception",
                "exception_type": type(e).__name__,
                "exception_module": type(e).__module__,
                "message": str(e)[:500],
            }
        app["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3)
        # Let streams closed by garbage collection end their spans.
        gc.collect()
        flush()
        fake_log = fake.log.entries()
    spans = [span_to_dict(s) for s in exporter.get_finished_spans()]
    t = truth.derive(fake_log, app)
    return {
        "truth": {
            **t,
            "scenario": scenario_id,
            "expected": scenario.expected,
            "expected_mismatch": truth.check_expected(scenario.expected, t),
            "app": app,
            "fake_log": fake_log,
        },
        "trace": {"library": library, "versions": _versions(library), "spans": spans},
    }


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    library, scenario_id, out_path = argv
    try:
        payload = {"ok": True, "observation": run(library, scenario_id)}
    except BaseException:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported as NOT RUN by the parent
        payload = {"ok": False, "error": traceback.format_exc(limit=8)}
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(payload, f, default=str)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""trueup sweep <library>: run the plain-SDK scenarios against one library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario, venvs
from trueup.runner.run import not_run
from trueup.scenarios import plain_sdk


def new_run_id(library: str) -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ") + f"-{library}"


def summary_line(r: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    sid = r["scenario"]
    if r["status"] != RAN:
        return f"{sid:30} NOT RUN  {r['reason']}"
    t, tr = r["observation"]["truth"], r["observation"]["trace"]
    app = t["app"]["outcome"] if t["outcome"] == "ok" else f"raised {t['exception']}"
    spans = ", ".join(f"{s['name']}={s['status']['code']}" for s in tr["spans"]) or "none"
    line = f"{sid:30} ran {r['seconds']:5.1f}s  app {app}; fake calls {t['calls']}; spans {len(tr['spans'])}: {spans}"
    if t["expected_mismatch"]:
        line += f"  [truth differs from scenario expectation: {', '.join(t['expected_mismatch'])}]"
    return line


def sweep(
    root: Path,
    library: str,
    *,
    ensure: Callable[[Path, str], Path] = venvs.ensure,
    run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_scenario,
    out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
) -> tuple[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    run_id = new_run_id(library)
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    started = time.monotonic()
    scenarios = plain_sdk()
    try:
        out(f"preparing venv for {library}")
        python: Path | None = ensure(root, library)
        venv_error = None
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - every scenario is reported NOT RUN
        python, venv_error = None, f"venv not ready: {e}"
    results = []
    for s in scenarios:
        r = not_run(s.id, library, venv_error) if python is None else run(python, library, s.id)
        results.append(r)
        out(summary_line(r))
        (run_dir / f"{s.id}.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1, default=str))
    ran = sum(r["status"] == RAN for r in results)
    lines = [
        f"trueup sweep {library}  run {run_id}",
        f"scenarios: {len(results)}  ran: {ran}  not run: {len(results) - ran}  "
        f"time: {time.monotonic() - started:.0f} s",
        "Truth and trace are recorded here; comparing them is not built yet.",
        "",
        *(summary_line(r) for r in results),
    ]
    (run_dir / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    (run_dir / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "scenarios": [{"id": r["scenario"], "status": r["status"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results],
    }, indent=1))
    out(f"ran {ran}/{len(results)}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return run_dir, results


def exit_code(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    # 2 (could not run) if anything was NOT RUN; mismatches are not judged yet.
    return 2 if any(r["status"] == NOT_RUN for r in results) else 0

"""Regression tests for traps hit while building the earlier harness."""

import asyncio
import inspect

import openai
import pytest

from trueup.fake import FakeProvider
from trueup.runner import apps, setups
from trueup.runner.run import child_env
from trueup.scenarios import library as lib

M = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]


# Trap 1: two scenarios reusing a response id made a library skip a span.


def test_response_ids_unique_across_calls_and_apis():
    with FakeProvider() as f:
        oc = openai.OpenAI(api_key="x", base_url=f.openai_base_url, max_retries=0)
        for _ in range(3):
            oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-plain", messages=M)
            oc.responses.create(model="resp-plain", input="hi")
            list(oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-plain", messages=M, stream=True))
        ids = [e["response_id"] for e in f.log.entries()]
    assert len(ids) == 9 and len(set(ids)) == 9


def test_response_ids_unique_across_fake_instances():
    seen = []
    for _ in range(2):
        with FakeProvider() as f:
            oc = openai.OpenAI(api_key="x", base_url=f.openai_base_url, max_retries=0)
            seen.append(oc.chat.completions.create(model="chat-plain", messages=M).id)
    # Each scenario runs in its own fake; the per-instance token keeps ids apart.
    assert seen[0] != seen[1]


def test_every_built_scenario_run_gets_its_own_ids():
    ids = []
    for s in lib.SCENARIOS:
        with FakeProvider() as f:
            try:
                apps.APPS[s.app](f.base_url, s.model)
            except Exception:
                pass
            ids += [e["response_id"] for e in f.log.entries() if e["response_id"]]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))


# Trap 2: one async client reused across asyncio.run loops gives "Event loop is closed".


def test_reused_async_client_across_loops_fails():
    # Documents the trap: this is what the apps must not do.
    with FakeProvider() as f:
        c = openai.AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url=f.openai_base_url, max_retries=0)

        async def call():
            return await c.chat.completions.create(model="chat-plain", messages=M)

        asyncio.run(call())
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="Event loop is closed"):
            asyncio.run(call())


@pytest.mark.parametrize("app", ["chat_async_stream", "an_async_create"])
def test_async_apps_survive_repeated_asyncio_run(app):
    with FakeProvider() as f:
        first = apps.APPS[app](f.base_url, "chat-plain" if app.startswith("chat") else "anth-plain")
        second = apps.APPS[app](f.base_url, "chat-plain" if app.startswith("chat") else "anth-plain")
    assert first == second


def test_apps_module_keeps_no_client_at_module_level():
    src = inspect.getsource(apps)
    top_level = [ln for ln in src.splitlines() if ln and not ln[0].isspace()]
    assert not any("OpenAI(" in ln or "Anthropic(" in ln for ln in top_level)


# Trap 3: a fake that sends no usage makes missing tokens look like a bug.


def test_stream_without_include_usage_records_tokens_as_not_sent():
    with FakeProvider() as f:
        apps.chat_stream(f.base_url, "chat-plain")
        (e,) = f.log.entries()
    assert e["usage"] is None and e["usage_sent"] is False


def test_scenarios_expect_no_tokens_only_where_fake_sends_none():
    # Expected tokens must come from what the fake really sent, so a trace
    # without tokens is only a bug when the fake did send them.
    s = lib.get("oa-chat-stream-no-usage")
    assert s.expected["tokens"] == [None]
    assert lib.get("oa-chat-stream-usage").expected["tokens"] == [lib.OA_TOK]


def test_fake_sends_usage_for_every_complete_reply_that_has_it():
    with FakeProvider() as f:
        apps.chat_create(f.base_url, "chat-plain")
        apps.chat_stream_usage(f.base_url, "chat-plain")
        apps.resp_stream(f.base_url, "resp-plain")
        apps.an_stream_helper(f.base_url, "anth-plain")
        entries = f.log.entries()
    assert all(e["usage_sent"] and e["usage"]["total_tokens"] > 0 for e in entries)


# Trap 4: neatlogs exporting to a dead endpoint made one run take 200 s.


def test_neatlogs_setup_disables_export_and_sets_no_endpoint():
    kw = setups.neatlogs_init_kwargs(tracer_provider=object())
    assert kw["disable_export"] is True
    assert "endpoint" not in kw
    assert kw["api_key"] == "trueup-fake"


def test_child_env_disables_export_and_drops_real_keys():
    env = child_env({"NEATLOGS_API_KEY": "real", "NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT": "http://127.0.0.1:9", "PATH": "/bin"})
    assert env["NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT"] == "true"
    assert "NEATLOGS_API_KEY" not in env and "NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT" not in env
    assert env["OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER"] == "none"
    assert env["TRACELOOP_TELEMETRY"] == "false"

"""Runner and sweep, offline. Subprocess runs against real venvs are in test_e2e.py."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from trueup.cli import EXIT_ERROR, EXIT_OK
from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario
from trueup.runner.run import SRC, child_env
from trueup.scenarios import plain_sdk
from trueup.sweep import exit_code, summary_line, sweep


def test_child_env_points_at_source_tree():
    env = child_env({})
    assert env["PYTHONPATH"] == str(SRC)
    assert (Path(env["PYTHONPATH"]) / "trueup" / "runner" / "child.py").exists()


def test_not_built_scenario_is_not_run_with_reason():
    r = run_scenario(Path(sys.executable), "neatlogs", "lg-agent")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "not_built" in r["reason"]


def test_unknown_scenario_is_not_run():
    r = run_scenario(Path(sys.executable), "neatlogs", "nope")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "unknown scenario" in r["reason"]


def test_missing_python_is_not_run():
    r = run_scenario(Path("/nonexistent/python"), "neatlogs", "oa-chat-plain")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "could not start" in r["reason"]


def test_library_import_failure_is_not_run(tmp_path):
    # This interpreter has no neatlogs, so setup fails inside the child.
    r = run_scenario(Path(sys.executable), "neatlogs", "oa-chat-plain", timeout=60)
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN
    assert "neatlogs" in r["reason"]


def test_child_crash_without_output_is_not_run(tmp_path):
    bad = tmp_path / "python"
    bad.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho boom >&2\nexit 3\n")
    bad.chmod(0o755)
    r = run_scenario(bad, "neatlogs", "oa-chat-plain")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "exited 3" in r["reason"] and "boom" in r["reason"]


def _fake_obs(sid):
    return {
        "scenario": sid, "library": "x", "status": RAN, "reason": None, "seconds": 1.0,
        "observation": {
            "truth": {"calls": 1, "outcome": "ok", "app": {"outcome": "ok"}, "expected_mismatch": []},
            "trace": {"spans": [{"name": "chat", "status": {"code": "OK"}}]},
        },
    }


def test_sweep_writes_one_file_per_scenario_and_summary(tmp_path):
    run_dir, results = sweep(
        tmp_path, "openinference",
        ensure=lambda root, lib: Path("/py"),
        run=lambda py, lib, sid: _fake_obs(sid),
        out=lambda s: None,
    )
    ids = [s.id for s in plain_sdk()]
    assert [r["scenario"] for r in results] == ids
    assert run_dir.parent == tmp_path / ".trueup" / "runs"
    for sid in ids:
        assert json.loads((run_dir / f"{sid}.json").read_text())["status"] == RAN
    summary = (run_dir / "summary.txt").read_text()
    assert f"ran: {len(ids)}" in summary and "not run: 0" in summary
    assert exit_code(results) == EXIT_OK


def test_sweep_venv_failure_reports_every_scenario_not_run(tmp_path):
    def broken(root, lib):
        raise RuntimeError("no network")

    run_dir, results = sweep(tmp_path, "neatlogs", ensure=broken, run=None, out=lambda s: None)
    assert len(results) == len(plain_sdk())
    assert all(r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "no network" in r["reason"] for r in results)
    assert "NOT RUN" in (run_dir / "summary.txt").read_text()
    assert exit_code(results) == EXIT_ERROR


def test_summary_line_flags_expectation_drift():
    r = _fake_obs("a")
    r["observation"]["truth"]["expected_mismatch"] = ["tokens"]
    assert "tokens" in summary_line(r)

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from trueup.cli import EXIT_ERROR, EXIT_OK
from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario
from trueup.runner.run import SRC, child_env
from trueup.scenarios import plain_sdk
from trueup.sweep import exit_code, summary_line, sweep


def test_child_env_points_at_source_tree():
    env = child_env({})
    assert env["PYTHONPATH"] == str(SRC)
    assert (Path(env["PYTHONPATH"]) / "trueup" / "runner" / "child.py").exists()


def test_not_built_scenario_is_not_run_with_reason():
    r = run_scenario(Path(sys.executable), "neatlogs", "lg-agent")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "not_built" in r["reason"]


def test_unknown_scenario_is_not_run():
    r = run_scenario(Path(sys.executable), "neatlogs", "nope")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "unknown scenario" in r["reason"]


def test_missing_python_is_not_run():
    r = run_scenario(Path("/nonexistent/python"), "neatlogs", "oa-chat-plain")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "could not start" in r["reason"]


def test_library_import_failure_is_not_run(tmp_path):
    # This interpreter has no neatlogs, so setup fails inside the child.
    r = run_scenario(Path(sys.executable), "neatlogs", "oa-chat-plain", timeout=60)
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN
    assert "neatlogs" in r["reason"]


def test_child_crash_without_output_is_not_run(tmp_path):
    bad = tmp_path / "python"
    bad.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho boom >&2\nexit 3\n")
    bad.chmod(0o755)
    r = run_scenario(bad, "neatlogs", "oa-chat-plain")
    assert r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "exited 3" in r["reason"] and "boom" in r["reason"]


def _fake_obs(sid):
    return {
        "scenario": sid, "library": "x", "status": RAN, "reason": None, "seconds": 1.0,
        "observation": {
            "truth": {"calls": 1, "outcome": "ok", "app": {"outcome": "ok"}, "expected_mismatch": []},
            "trace": {"spans": [{"name": "chat", "status": {"code": "OK"}}]},
        },
    }


def test_sweep_writes_one_file_per_scenario_and_summary(tmp_path):
    run_dir, results = sweep(
        tmp_path, "openinference",
        ensure=lambda root, lib: Path("/py"),
        run=lambda py, lib, sid: _fake_obs(sid),
        out=lambda s: None,
    )
    ids = [s.id for s in plain_sdk()]
    assert [r["scenario"] for r in results] == ids
    assert run_dir.parent == tmp_path / ".trueup" / "runs"
    for sid in ids:
        assert json.loads((run_dir / f"{sid}.json").read_text())["status"] == RAN
    summary = (run_dir / "summary.txt").read_text()
    assert f"ran: {len(ids)}" in summary and "not run: 0" in summary
    assert exit_code(results) == EXIT_OK


def test_sweep_venv_failure_reports_every_scenario_not_run(tmp_path):
    def broken(root, lib):
        raise RuntimeError("no network")

    run_dir, results = sweep(tmp_path, "neatlogs", ensure=broken, run=None, out=lambda s: None)
    assert len(results) == len(plain_sdk())
    assert all(r["status"] == NOT_RUN and "no network" in r["reason"] for r in results)
    assert "NOT RUN" in (run_dir / "summary.txt").read_text()
    assert exit_code(results) == EXIT_ERROR


def test_summary_line_flags_expectation_drift():
    r = _fake_obs("a")
    r["observation"]["truth"]["expected_mismatch"] = ["tokens"]
    assert "tokens" in summary_line(r)

content.text:
The fake provider, scenario library, runner and `trueup sweep` are built, and all three libraries ran all 31 plain-SDK scenarios. Nothing was committed.

**Tests**
- `uv run pytest -q`: 104 passed (offline, about 9 s).
- `uv run pytest -q -m e2e`: 9 passed (about 22 s). This covers the venv and subprocess tests across the three libraries, including a neatlogs run that must finish in under 30 s.

**Sweeps**

| Library | Ran | NOT RUN |
|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 31/31 (≈97 s) | 0 |
| openinference | 31/31 (≈71 s) | 0 |
| openllmetry | 31/31 (≈114 s) | 0 |

The first openllmetry sweep was 0/31 NOT RUN, and I've left that run directory in place. The cause was `traceloop-sdk` importing `httpx` without declaring it, and this `openai` version doesn't pull `httpx` in. I added `httpx` to that library's venv packages, and the second sweep ran 31/31. NOT RUN reasons are now the final error line, with the full traceback kept in the JSON.

**What's in place**
- **Fake provider** (`src/trueup/fake/`): all the requested formats, with the scenario chosen by model name. Every id is unique per call and per fake instance. The truth log records each request, what was sent back, and the tokens per call, or that no usage was sent.
- **Fixture tests:** 34, using the real `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs. Two behaviours don't meet the "raise the SDK's own exception" rule. I recorded them as they are rather than hiding them:
  - The `openai` SDK hands a Responses `error` event to the app instead of raising.
  - The `anthropic` SDK lets a dropped stream through as a raw `RemoteProtocolError`. A dropped non-streamed call does raise `APIConnectionError`.
- **Scenarios:** 31 plain-SDK cases: 12 chat, 9 Responses, 10 Anthropic. A unit test runs each app with no tracing library and checks the expected truth against what really happens; it caught one wrong expectation of mine. The 20 LangChain/LangGraph/OpenAI Agents cases are listed but **not built**.
- **Traps:** all four have regression tests. The async-client trap is reproduced against the fake ("Event loop is closed"). For neatlogs I use `neatlogs.init` with `disable_export=True` and pass in my own tracer provider, so no endpoint is ever set.

**Leads for the comparison step** (seen in the sweeps, not judged yet):
- **neatlogs** adds `stream_options.include_usage` to the app's streamed chat requests. As a result, the three "no usage" scenarios flag that the truth differs from the scenario's expectation; that comes from the library changing the request, not from the harness.
- **openinference** exports no span when the app closes a stream early, or when a Responses stream ends with an error event.
- **openllmetry**:
  - Chat streams that raised (error event, dropped connection) are marked OK.
  - No span is exported for Responses failed or incomplete.
  - No span is exported for Anthropic stream errors or cuts.

Dated entries are in `hackathon.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and I updated the README's status section.

Two claude.ai connectors, Paybox and arvix mcp, need authorising in your claude.ai connector settings; they're unavailable until then. Nothing in this task used them.
